caption:
India just finished a 1,000 MW battery that isn't a battery at all. It stores energy by pumping water uphill.

THDC India completed the 1,000 MW Tehri Pumped Storage Project in Uttarakhand on April 12, 2026, using the existing Tehri and Koteshwar reservoirs as a closed-loop system. The plant pumps water uphill when power is cheap, then releases it downhill to generate electricity during peak demand. Built at a cost of roughly Rs 8,339 crore across four 250 MW units, it brings the full Tehri hydro complex to 2,400 MW total.

Everyone's racing to build lithium-ion storage. This one just moves water instead - and it's already finished.

Sources: Renewable Watch, Electrical Mirror (2026)
